detailed_description: CSS Unit Converter converts one value into every other supported CSS length unit at once. Type a numeric value, pick the source unit from px, rem, em, pt, vw, vh, or %, then set the base font size (default 16) and assumed viewport width and height (default 1920 x 1080). The result panel reactively shows the same value rendered in all seven units, using the fixed conversions px<->rem/em via base font size, 1pt = 1.333px, vw/vh = percent of the viewport dimensions, and % treated against the base font size. There is no Convert button, target-unit checkboxes, copy button, tooltips, multi-row conversion matrix, or media-query/container-context simulation.
usage_steps: Type the numeric value into the value input
Pick the source unit from the dropdown (px, rem, em, pt, vw, vh, or %)
Set the base font size in px (default 16) used for rem, em, and % conversions
Set the viewport width and height in px (default 1920 and 1080) used for vw and vh conversions
Read the result panel, which shows the same value converted into every supported unit
Note that em and rem share the same base font size and that % is computed against that base
usage_examples: See what 1.5rem becomes in px when the base font size is set to 10
Convert 24pt to px using the fixed 1pt = 1.333px ratio
Compare how 50vw maps to px at a 1920-wide vs 768-wide viewport
Translate a px value into rem and em while keeping the base font size aligned with your stylesheet
